source: independent (non-author) pred-scout-coach-critic reviewing data/postgame/*.json coaching against the match facts; preference-based / ungrounded lines flagged; grounded rewrites applied back

4dea0473-d3c5-444d-b8ef-e9b015ab43ab.quote: Down four towers before we had touched one of theirs, with two Fangtooths and a Genesis Core gone the same way, the map was theirs. Then the buildings started falling the other way: both Primal Fangtooths, Orb Prime, three inhibitors and the Core. Three of our four won fights turned straight into an objective or structure, while they turned half of their ten into anything. That conversion is the story of the win.
4dea0473-d3c5-444d-b8ef-e9b015ab43ab.issue: causal overclaim: much of the comeback (their Outer Tower in the lost 25.9 fight window, the first Primal Fangtooth in the lost 28.4 fight window) came without a won fight, so won-fight conversion is not the whole story
4dea0473-d3c5-444d-b8ef-e9b015ab43ab.rewrite: Down four towers before we had touched one of theirs, with two Fangtooths and a Genesis Core gone the same way, the map was theirs. Then the buildings fell the other way: both Primal Fangtooths, Orb Prime, three inhibitors and the Core. Three of our four won fights became an objective or structure; they converted half of their ten. We also took a tower and the first Primal Fangtooth in the same windows as fights we lost. Taking the map, more than winning fights, is how this flipped.

4dea0473-d3c5-444d-b8ef-e9b015ab43ab.quote: Iggy & Scorch owned the biggest fight of the game: Argus, Terra and Khaimera in one exchange, then two of their inner towers and an inhibitor fell. Damage ran about a third above his usual on the hero, and he took the last kill before the Core. Terra was the recurring problem, credited with three of his five deaths. While Terra still has Unstoppable Force, hold Inferno's knockback until she spends it, since it cleanses and adds tenacity.
4dea0473-d3c5-444d-b8ef-e9b015ab43ab.issue: mechanic reasoning misleads: catalog cleanse happens on cast, then the ult grants tenacity for several seconds, so the tenacity argues against knocking her back right after she spends it
4dea0473-d3c5-444d-b8ef-e9b015ab43ab.rewrite: Iggy & Scorch owned the biggest fight of the game: Argus, Terra and Khaimera in one exchange, then two of their inner towers and an inhibitor fell. Damage ran about a third above his usual on the hero, and he took the last kill before the Core. Terra was the recurring problem, credited with three of his five deaths. Terra's ultimate cleanses on cast and then adds tenacity, so Iggy & Scorch lands Inferno's knockback once that tenacity window ends.

4dea0473-d3c5-444d-b8ef-e9b015ab43ab.quote: Goldilocks324 ran the most complete game on our side, and it was not fucking close. Gideon beat his own usual farm and damage on the hero, finished richest in the lobby, and took kills off four different enemies, Legion three times. That is the standard. Argus was the recurring problem, credited with two of his four deaths. When Argus has not shown and Gideon has to cross the map, keep the portal for the exit, not the next engage.
4dea0473-d3c5-444d-b8ef-e9b015ab43ab.issue: selective: Khaimera also killed Gideon twice, so Argus alone is not 'the' recurring problem; the sentence also duplicates the Iggy & Scorch 'recurring problem, credited with N of his M deaths' template

4dea0473-d3c5-444d-b8ef-e9b015ab43ab.quote: Knell shreds both armors with each hero hit and hands Maco part of what it shreds, so it pays when he is in the fight hitting heroes. Patina's shield only rebuilds after a stretch without taking damage, so it is a between-fights cushion. Resonant Repair heals and grants tenacity whenever he is immobilized, which fits Khaimera's stun and Argus's control. The field mostly runs Exarch on Maco; this match cannot say whether it would have done more.
4dea0473-d3c5-444d-b8ef-e9b015ab43ab.issue: 'mostly' overstates field data: Exarch is the most common Maco support Eternal but under half of recorded games
